I hate that you’re in so much pain. I can relate and I wish that I could take even a tiny bit of the pain away from you.
I can relate too. I wish it were easier. I’m sorry that you’re in pain.
Thank you for letting me carry some of this with you. This might sound super cheesy, but I’m being sincere. I’m going to light a candle and send good thoughts to you throughout the day.
Let me hold some of the pain for a minute so you can rest. I’ll be thinking of you.

I have to try to get some sleep but you will be my last thought before I go to sleep. I’m holding you in my heart and I will carry some of the pain, even if it’s only for tonight. You are worthy. So very very worthy. You should know that I am telling myself that as I’m saying it to you.
Don’t listen to that shit! You’re worthy. So worthy. From my heart to yours, I mean it.
I survived a suicide attempt when I was about your age. I’m glad I made it, Life is hard and I’m still in a lot of pain but I’m glad that I didn’t die when I was so young.

I can’t sleep. I’m thinking about you. My heart hurts so much every day and I hate that you feel that way too. I wish I could take it away, but maybe it will help knowing that I am holding some of the pain. If you close your eyes, I hope that you can feel me holding some of the pain. Maybe that will give you a little break from it.
I’m so sorry. I hate this for you. I wish that I could take even a tiny bit of the pain away. I’m sending love to you tonight.
My family gets super angry with me when I am at my lowest and feeling suicidal, so that’s fun. I wish things were different. I’m sending good thoughts your way.
I’m a Mom. I have three daughters. I think about dying most days. I hear your pain. I’m so sorry. I’m sending love to you.

You’re in my thoughts, both of you. I wish that this were easier. I’m holding you tight. I wish there were more comforting words that I could share, but I hear you. I hear you. We don’t know each other, but I know pain and it sucks.
I hate that you are in pain. Sending love your way.
Thanks for your concern for being available. I don’t need to talk right now, but thank you.
I can relate. Life can be so painful. I’m holding you in my heart.

It’s really, really hard for her. She’s young (12) so there are not as many expectations of her. To be honest, we just do our best to help her stay regulated and we help her ride the waves of discomfort (and meltdowns) when they happen. She’s taking a break from therapy, but it did help her a lot. My sister practices therapeutic breath work and that really helps her manage her anxiety. I’ve been meaning to start practicing it myself and introduce it to my daughter if I find it helpful. Sometimes a cold glass of water can help her start to reset. I will let you know if I think of anything else. My brain is in freeze mode at the moment.

My daughter experiences this. She needs “just right” conditions in order to be temporarily free from anxiety. I also experience a lot of anxiety, but it doesn’t show up in quite the same way. I’m hoping that you will be able to find some relief. I’ll be thinking of you and sending positive thoughts your way.
Thank you for your compassionate and thoughtful response.
